content.title: About
content.content: Plain potato chips are thinly sliced potatoes that are fried until crisp and lightly salted. They have a characteristic salty taste, a light buttery texture, and are a popular snack worldwide.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial brand of chips appeared in the United States in 1853.
More than 300 potato varieties are used for chip production, but high‑starch types are most common.
In the 1960s chips began to be packaged in airtight bags, extending shelf life.
The world’s largest bag of chips weighed over 1,000 kg and was made in Japan.
In some countries chips are flavored with unusual seasonings such as wasabi or truffle sea salt.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: Potato chips provide carbohydrates that quickly supply the body with energy.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: A small amount of vitamin C remains when chips are fried properly, supporting the immune system.

items.title: Potassium
items.content: Potatoes are rich in potassium, important for fluid balance and muscle function.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Potatoes contain carotenoids and polyphenols that may protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Excess sodium can raise blood pressure, so moderation is advised.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Chips are high in fat and calories, which can contribute to weight gain if eaten frequently.

items.title: Trans fats
items.content: Frying in certain oils can create trans fats, which are detrimental to cardiovascular health.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: Rarely, some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to potatoes.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Chips are convenient as a standalone snack, added to salads, used as a garnish for soups, or incorporated into dishes for added crunch. Choose versions without excessive flavorings for a healthier option.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store chips in a sealed package in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, transfer them to an airtight container to maintain crispness.
